records.name: Japanese Government (MEXT) Scholarship
records.providerName: Japan Student Services Organization (JASSO) / Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology (MEXT)
records.summary: The Japanese Government (MEXT) Scholarship supports international students through embassy or university recommendation across research, undergraduate, teacher training, Japanese studies, college of technology, specialized training college and Young Leaders Program tracks. The official page states tuition is exempted, monthly scholarship payments are provided, and round-trip airfare is provided.
records.sourceNotes: The page describes seven program types with different levels and fields; only the explicitly stated bachelor, master and doctoral levels are mapped. It does not enumerate all eligible nationalities or provide an exhaustive field list.
records.evidence: Scholarship: ¥143,000–145,000 per month, ¥117,000 per month, or ¥242,000 per month depending on program type. Tuition: exempted. Travel allowance: round-trip travel expenses (airfare) provided.

records.name: JASSO Monbukagakusho Honors Scholarship for Privately Financed International Students
records.summary: This JASSO scholarship supports privately financed international students enrolled in Japanese universities, graduate schools, junior colleges, colleges of technology, specialized training colleges, preparatory courses and Japanese language institutions who have strong academic records and financial difficulties. The official page states monthly amounts of 48,000 yen for university and graduate-level students and 30,000 yen for Japanese language institutions.
records.sourceTitle: Monbukagakusho Honors Scholarship for Privately Financed International Students
records.sourceNotes: The source lists several institution types beyond bachelor, master and doctoral study; only the degree levels explicitly named on the page are mapped. Eligibility is based on enrolment and financial need rather than a listed set of nationalities.
records.evidence: Graduate schools (doctoral, master's), research students at graduate level, undergraduate universities and other listed institutions: 48,000 yen per month. Japanese language institutions: 30,000 yen per month. Payment is generally one year from April to March, or six months from October to March.

records.name: JASSO Student Exchange Support Program (Scholarship for Study in Japan under Agreement)
records.summary: JASSO offers this scholarship to qualified international students admitted to a Japanese university, graduate school, junior college, college of technology or specialized training college under a short-term student exchange agreement. The official page states a monthly amount of 80,000 yen for exchanges lasting from 8 days to 1 year.
records.sourceTitle: Student Exchange Support Program (Scholarship for Study in Japan under Agreement)
records.sourceNotes: Eligible countries and regions are stated as countries with diplomatic relations with Japan, plus Taiwan and Palestine, but the page does not enumerate them; nationalityScope is therefore UNKNOWN. Degree levels reflect the university and graduate-school categories named on the source.
records.evidence: Monthly amount: 80,000 yen. Payment period: from 8 days to 1 year. Eligible recipients include students accepted under a short-term exchange agreement who cannot participate solely at their own expense for financial reasons and who will return to their home institution.

records.name: GKS (Global Korea Scholarship) Degree Program
records.summary: The GKS Degree Program is a Korean government-invited scholarship for outstanding international students pursuing associate, bachelor's, master's or doctoral degrees in Korea. The official page states benefits include airfare, Korean language training fees, tuition and monthly allowances, with separate undergraduate and graduate tracks.
records.sourceNotes: The source includes associate degree programs but does not use one of the available degree enums for that level, so it is noted here rather than mapped. Fields are described as various fields such as humanities, social studies, natural sciences, and arts and physical education, with etc.; this is not an exhaustive list.
records.evidence: Scholarship Benefits: Airfare, Korean language training fees, tuition, and monthly allowances. Scholarship Duration: Korean language training (1 year) plus associate degree programs (2–3 years), bachelor's degree programs (4–6 years), master's degrees (2 years), doctoral degrees (3 years). Nationality: applicants and both parents must hold non-Korean citizenship.

records.name: GKS Exchange Students Program
records.summary: The GKS Exchange Students Program supports international undergraduate and graduate students enrolled at overseas universities with exchange agreements with participating Korean universities. The official page states a monthly allowance of KRW 630,000 and round-trip economy airfare for a four-month exchange semester.
records.sourceNotes: Eligibility is based on foreign nationality, enrolment at a partner overseas university and academic performance, not an enumerated country list. The source does not state field-of-study restrictions.
records.evidence: Scholarship Duration: 4 months (1 semester). Selection Quota: approximately 500 international students, subject to budget changes. Monthly Allowance: KRW 630,000 per month, which may vary based on stay and semester end date. Round-trip Airfare: economy class airfare based on actual cost.

records.name: Korea-Japan Future Talent Invitational Program
records.summary: The Korea-Japan Future Talent Invitational Program selects Japanese nationals for bachelor's or associate degree study in Korea. The official page states support for one year of Korean language training plus 4–6 years for a bachelor's degree or 2–3 years for an associate degree, with tuition, language training expenses, an academic allowance and round-trip airfare.
records.sourceNotes: The source also includes associate degree study, which is not mapped to the available degree enums. Fields of study are stated as all fields.
records.evidence: Number of Students: up to 20 students annually. Fields of Study: all fields. Eligibility: Japanese nationals under 25 years of age who have graduated from high school. Scholarships Benefits: tuition fees, language training expenses, academic allowance and round-trip airfare.

records.name: K-Arts AMA+ Scholarship Program for Developing Countries' Artistic Talent
records.summary: The Korea National University of Arts AMA+ Scholarship Program supports outstanding artistic talent from OECD DAC recipient countries for undergraduate or graduate study in Korea. The official Study in Korea page lists support including airfare, a monthly living allowance, Korean language training, tuition fees and medical insurance.
records.sourceTitle: Korea National University of Arts (K-Arts) AMA+ Scholarship Program for Developing Countries' Artistic Talent
records.sourceNotes: The source refers to 140 OECD DAC recipient countries but does not enumerate them, so nationalityScope is UNKNOWN. It states undergraduate and graduate programs without subdividing graduate into master's or doctoral; only the explicitly listed bachelor and master levels are mapped.
records.evidence: Supported Fields: Arts (Music, Dance, Fine Arts, Film, Theater, Korean Traditional Arts). Programs: Undergraduate and Graduate. Support Details: Airfare, Monthly Living Allowance, Korean Language Training, Tuition Fees, Medical Insurance, etc. Application Period: March.

records.name: POSCO TJ Park Foundation Scholarships for Asian Students Studying in Korea
records.summary: The POSCO TJ Park Foundation scholarship supports Asian nationals enrolling in master's or doctoral programs in Korea. The official Study in Korea page lists tuition, living expenses, an arrival allowance and language excellence scholarships, and states that all academic fields except MBA are supported.
records.sourceTitle: POSCO TJ Park Foundation (Scholarships for Asian Students Studying in Korea)
records.sourceNotes: The source says Asian nationals but does not enumerate eligible countries, so nationalityScope is UNKNOWN. Supported fields are stated as all academic fields excluding MBA.
records.evidence: Number of Students: 50 students. Application Period: May. Eligible Programs: Asian nationals planning to enroll in Master's or Doctoral programs in the following academic year. Supported Fields: all academic fields excluding MBA. Support Details: tuition, living expenses, arrival allowance, language excellence scholarships.

records.name: Korea Foundation (KF) Fellowship for Korean Studies Graduate Students
records.summary: The Korea Foundation Fellowship supports graduate students in Korean Studies from more than 30 countries. The official Study in Korea page states support for tuition fees, with the amount varying by region, country and local cost of living, for a duration of one year.
records.sourceTitle: Korea Foundation (KF Fellowship for Korean Studies Graduate Students)
records.sourceNotes: The source says students come from over 30 countries but does not enumerate them, so nationalityScope is UNKNOWN. Support is stated as tuition fees with an amount that varies by region, country and local cost of living.
records.evidence: Number of Students: approximately 150 students worldwide per year. Duration of Support: 1 year. Supported Fields: Master's and Doctoral programs in Korean Studies from over 30 countries. Support Details: tuition fees, amount varies by region, country and local cost of living.

records.name: Hong Kong PhD Fellowship Scheme
records.providerName: Research Grants Council, University Grants Committee Hong Kong
records.summary: The Hong Kong PhD Fellowship Scheme aims to attract outstanding researchers to full-time PhD study at Hong Kong universities. The official page states 400 fellowships for 2027/28 and, for 2026/27, an annual stipend of HK$344,400 plus annual conference and research-related travel allowances of HK$14,400 for up to three years.
records.sourcePublisher: Research Grants Council, University Grants Committee Hong Kong
records.sourceNotes: The source invites applicants from all over but does not enumerate nationalities. It describes two assessment panels rather than an exhaustive list of eligible fields. The 2027/28 call is stated as opening 1 September 2026 and closing 1 December 2026. Hong Kong SAR is mapped to CN because the platform country list has no separate HK code.
records.evidence: 400 PhD Fellowships will be granted in the 2027/28 academic year. In the 2026/27 academic year, each awardee is entitled to an annual stipend of HK$344,400 and annual conference and research-related travel allowances of HK$14,400 for a period of up to three years. Applicants from all over, seeking admission as a new full-time PhD student in a Hong Kong university, are eligible.

records.name: Scholarship Programme for Diaspora Children (SPDC)
records.providerName: Ministry of External Affairs, Government of India
records.summary: The Scholarship Programme for Diaspora Children makes undergraduate higher education in Indian universities accessible to children of Persons of Indian Origin, Non-resident Indians and Indian workers in ECR countries. The official page states scholarships up to US$4,000 per annum toward tuition, hostel, admission and other fees except food charges.
records.sourcePublisher: Ministry of External Affairs, Government of India
records.sourceNotes: The scheme applies in selected 69 countries but the page does not enumerate all of them; it only lists ECR countries for one eligibility category. The field list is non-exhaustive because the source says 'and some other courses'.
records.evidence: Ministry offered 150 scholarship every year under the Scheme, out of which 50 are reserved for PIOs, 50 for NRIs and 50 for children of Indian workers in ECR countries. Students are awarded scholarship up to US$4000 per annum towards payment of tuition fee, hostel fee, admission fee and other fee except food charges for under-graduate courses.

records.name: COMPEX Nepal Scholarship Scheme
records.summary: The COMPEX Nepal Scholarship Scheme is administered by the Embassy of India in Kathmandu for study in India in listed undergraduate courses. The official page states an age range of 16–23 years, application requirements and a selection test, but does not state financial coverage or award amounts.
records.sourceNotes: The source does not state the scholarship amount or what costs are covered, so fundingType is OTHER. It is a Nepal-specific scheme administered by the Embassy of India, but the page does not explicitly enumerate eligible nationalities beyond requiring a citizenship certificate.
records.evidence: Course: BE / B.Sc. (Agriculture) / B. Pharmaceutical / B.Sc. (Food Technology) / B.Sc. (Nursing). The minimum age required to apply is 16 years and the maximum age is 23 years. Selection is based on a qualifying/competitive test conducted by the Embassy of India.

records.name: ANU International Achievement Award
records.summary: The ANU International Achievement Award offers academically capable overseas students a tuition fee reduction of 20%, 25% or 50% for up to four years for undergraduate and postgraduate coursework study. Eligible students are automatically considered when they apply for admission.
records.sourceNotes: The source defines eligibility by exclusion of specific residential statuses rather than a positive nationality list, so nationalityScope is UNKNOWN. Field scope is stated as any eligible program except Doctor of Medicine and Surgery (MChD) and Master of Digital Transformation and Entrepreneurship (MDTE).
records.evidence: Value: 20%, 25% or 50% off tuition fees for up to 4 years. Study level: Undergraduate/Bachelor, Honours, Postgraduate/Masters, and Graduate certificate. Field of study: any eligible program except Doctor of Medicine and Surgery (MChD) and Master of Digital Transformation and Entrepreneurship (MDTE).

records.name: ANU Vice-Chancellor's International Achievement Award
records.summary: The ANU Vice-Chancellor's International Achievement Award provides a 20% reduction of first-year tuition fees for international students from specified East Asian countries and regions. The official page states automatic consideration for eligible applicants and payment for one year.
records.sourceNotes: ISO2 codes map the source's listed countries and regions: China, Taiwan, Japan, Mongolia, Republic of Korea and the Democratic People's Republic of Korea. The source's China wording also includes Hong Kong SAR and Macau SAR, which are not separate codes in the platform country list. Field scope is stated as any eligible program except MChD and MDTE.
records.evidence: Value: 20% off your first-year tuition fees. Duration: payment made for 1 year. Eligibility includes residential status in China (including Taiwan, Hong Kong SAR and Macau SAR), Japan, Mongolia, Republic of Korea and The Democratic People's Republic of Korea. Study level: Undergraduate/Bachelor, Honours, Postgraduate/Masters, and Graduate certificate.

records.name: UNSW Scientia PhD Scholarship Scheme
records.summary: The UNSW Scientia PhD Scholarship Scheme is a fully funded PhD scholarship for domestic applicants with global ambitions. The official page states a living allowance scholarship, a one-off Global Mobility Grant and 20 scholarships available for commencement in 2027.
records.sourceNotes: The source says the scheme is for domestic applicants but does not enumerate citizenship or residency categories, so nationalityScope is UNKNOWN. Projects span multiple faculties but no exhaustive eligible-field list is stated.
records.evidence: These projects are fully funded, and successful candidates will receive a living allowance scholarship and a one-off Global Mobility Grant to carry out international engagement activities. A total of 20 scholarships will be available for commencement in 2027.

records.name: A*STAR Graduate Scholarship
records.providerName: Agency for Science, Technology and Research (A*STAR)
records.summary: The A*STAR Graduate Scholarship supports PhD study at a Singapore autonomous university with research at an A*STAR Research Institute. The official page states full tuition fees, a monthly sustenance allowance, other allowances, up to 12 months of overseas attachment and funding for up to four years, and says the scholarship is open to applicants of all nationalities.
records.sourcePublisher: Agency for Science, Technology and Research (A*STAR)
records.sourceNotes: International applicants must have completed or be on track to obtain a Bachelor's or Master's degree at a Singapore Autonomous University. The source lists research areas but explicitly says the list is not exhaustive.
records.evidence: Open to applicants of all nationalities. Successful applicants will be given the following support for up to 4 years: full tuition fees, monthly sustenance allowance inclusive of CPF contribution where applicable, other allowances including book, computer, conference and thesis allowances, and support for up to 12 months of overseas attachment.

records.name: A*STAR National Science Scholarship (PhD)
records.providerName: Agency for Science, Technology and Research (A*STAR)
records.summary: The A*STAR National Science Scholarship (PhD) supports Singaporeans and other nationals intending to take up Singapore citizenship to pursue PhD study at a top overseas institution. The official page states full tuition fees, monthly allowances, annual return airfare and other allowances for up to five years, plus a one-year research attachment at A*STAR before the PhD.
records.sourcePublisher: Agency for Science, Technology and Research (A*STAR)
records.sourceNotes: Eligibility is nationality-plus-intent based rather than a fixed country list: applicants must be Singaporean or other nationals intending to take up Singapore citizenship, with non-Singaporeans obtaining Singapore Permanent Residence before studies and citizenship during the PhD. The research-area list is explicitly non-exhaustive.
records.evidence: Funding period: up to 5 years. Support includes full tuition fees, monthly sustenance allowance, monthly overseas living allowance, annual return airfare, conference, thesis, computer, settling-in and language programme allowances where applicable. Applicants must be Singaporean or other nationals intending to take up Singapore citizenship.

records.name: A*STAR International Fellowship
records.providerName: Agency for Science, Technology and Research (A*STAR)
records.summary: The A*STAR International Fellowship supports up to two years of overseas postdoctoral training at leading universities, research institutions or eligible deep-tech startups through Research and Innovation tracks. The official page states a monthly overseas living allowance, a monthly sustenance allowance, annual return airfare, other allowances and annual personal insurance, followed by a three-year service commitment.
records.sourcePublisher: Agency for Science, Technology and Research (A*STAR)
records.sourceNotes: This is a postdoctoral fellowship rather than a degree scholarship, so degreeLevels is empty. Eligibility is primarily Singaporean or Singapore Permanent Resident, with exceptional non-SPR foreigners considered only if they obtain Singapore citizenship before the fellowship; this is not a country list. The research-area list is explicitly non-exhaustive.
records.evidence: The successful applicant receives up to 2 years of overseas postdoctoral research training support: monthly overseas living allowance, monthly sustenance allowance inclusive of CPF contribution, annual return airfare, settling-in, computer and conference allowances, and annual personal insurance. Upon completion, scholars contribute to A*STAR or relevant organisations for 3 years.

records.name: A*STAR Research Attachment Programme
records.providerName: Agency for Science, Technology and Research (A*STAR)
records.summary: The A*STAR Research Attachment Programme enables overseas-based PhD students to conduct 1–2 years of jointly supervised research at A*STAR in Singapore. The official page lists a monthly stipend of S$3,600, housing allowance, airfare grant, settling-in allowance, IT allowance, visa costs, medical insurance and conference allowance, while explicitly stating that university tuition fees are not covered.
records.sourcePublisher: Agency for Science, Technology and Research (A*STAR)
records.sourceNotes: The source describes overseas-based PhD students jointly nominated by their home university and A*STAR supervisors but does not enumerate eligible nationalities. Research areas are broad and described with 'and more', so fieldScope is UNKNOWN.
records.evidence: Coverage includes monthly stipend S$3,600, monthly housing allowance S$300, one-time airfare grant S$1,500, one-time settling-in allowance S$1,000, one-time IT allowance S$800, visa cost, medical insurance and conference allowance. A*STAR does not cover university tuition fees during ARAP.

records.name: JSPS Postdoctoral Fellowships for Research in Japan
records.providerName: Japan Society for the Promotion of Science
records.summary: JSPS Postdoctoral Fellowships for Research in Japan provide opportunities for pre- and post-doctoral researchers from abroad to conduct cooperative research with leading Japanese research groups. The official overview page describes Summer, Short-term (PE), Short-term (PA), Standard and ended Strategic programs, but does not state financial coverage on that page.
records.sourcePublisher: Japan Society for the Promotion of Science
records.sourceTitle: Postdoctoral Fellowships for Research in Japan
records.sourceNotes: This is a research fellowship rather than a degree scholarship, so degreeLevels is empty. Nationality eligibility differs by program and the overview page gives groups rather than an exhaustive country list. Financial amounts are not stated on this fetched page, so fundingType is OTHER.
records.evidence: JSPS provides opportunities for pre-/post-doctoral researchers from abroad to engage in cooperative research under the guidance of their hosts with leading research groups in universities and other Japanese institutions. JSPS has several types of programs to accommodate researchers in every stage of their career.

records.name: NL Scholarship
records.summary: The NL Scholarship is for international students from outside the European Economic Area who want to pursue a full-time bachelor's or master's programme at a participating Dutch higher education institution. It provides €5,000 in the first year and is not a full-tuition scholarship; application deadlines are set by each institution.
records.sourceNotes: The official page states non-EEA nationality as the eligibility criterion but does not enumerate eligible countries; no country list was inferred.
records.evidence: The scholarship amounts to € 5,000. You will receive this in the first year of your studies. Please note that this is not a full-tuition scholarship.

records.name: France Excellence Eiffel Scholarship Program
records.providerName: French Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Campus France)
records.summary: The France Excellence Eiffel Scholarship Program supports outstanding foreign students in Master's, engineering and Doctoral/PhD programmes in seven priority fields. Master's holders receive €1,200 per month and doctoral holders €2,000 per month from January 2026, with travel and insurance services; tuition fees are not covered, and institutions submit applications.
records.sourceTitle: The France Excellence Eiffel scholarship program
records.evidence: The France Excellence Eiffel scholarship program is a tool developed by the French Ministry of Foreign Affairs to assist French institutions of higher education in attracting the best foreign students to Master's and Doctoral/Phd degree programs.

records.name: ICP Connect Scholarship
records.summary: VLIR-UOS ICP Connect scholarships fund accredited English-taught study programmes at Flemish universities and universities of applied sciences and arts for applicants from 25 eligible countries in Africa, Asia and Latin America. Awards cover tuition fees, travel, insurance and living expenses for the full 12-, 24- or 36-month programme duration.
records.sourceNotes: Eligible nationalities are taken from the linked official VLIR-UOS country-list page, which was also fetched; candidates must also reside in an eligible country at application. The scholarship supports bachelor's, initial master's and advanced master's programmes.
records.evidence: VLIRUOS ICP Connect scholarships cover tuition fees, travel, insurance and living expenses (board and lodging). We only offer scholarships for the full duration of the study programme (12/24/36 months).

records.name: Heinrich Böll Foundation Scholarships for Graduates and PhD Students
records.summary: The Heinrich Böll Foundation's scholarships support graduate students and PhD students from DAC countries who intend to pursue a Master's degree or PhD in Germany. International applicants must have completed their first degree abroad, with priority for those not yet resident in Germany; the foundation is funded by the Federal Ministry of Education and Research and the Federal Foreign Office.
records.sourceTitle: Tailwind for Talents: Scholarships for Graduates and PhD students
records.sourceNotes: The official page refers to DAC countries but does not enumerate them; no country list was inferred.
records.evidence: In our effort to foster equal opportunities and equitable access to education, we support graduate students and PhD students from DAC countries who intend to pursue a Master's degree or PhD in Germany.

records.name: Swiss Government Excellence Scholarships
records.providerName: Swiss Confederation (State Secretariat for Education, Research and Innovation)
records.summary: Swiss Government Excellence Scholarships 2027–2028 are awarded by the Swiss Confederation to early career researchers who have completed a Master's degree and to artists from a limited number of countries. Research scholarships are available in any discipline at Swiss institutions; the page states a maximum age of 35 and funding of CHF 2,450 per month, with applications opening on 20 August 2026.
records.sourcePublisher: State Secretariat for Education, Research and Innovation SERI
records.sourceNotes: The official page says the programme is open to applicants from 183 countries but does not list them; research scholarships are postgraduate research awards rather than a specified degree programme, while art scholarships are for an initial Master's degree.
records.evidence: Swiss Government Excellence Scholarships are mainly intended for talented early career researchers (ECRs) from abroad who have already completed their Master's degree. The scholarship programme is currently open to applicants from 183 countries.

records.name: Italian Government Scholarships for Foreign Students and Italian Citizens Living Abroad
records.providerName: Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation
records.summary: The Italian Government offers scholarships for foreign students and Italian citizens living abroad for the 2026-2027 academic year to foster cooperation in cultural, scientific and technological fields, promote Italian language and culture, and support Italy's economic system. Awards are for academic courses in Italy only, and applications must be submitted through the Study in Italy portal by 26 March 2026.
records.sourcePublisher: Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation
records.sourceTitle: Scholarships for foreign students and Italian citizens living abroad awarded by the Italian Government
records.sourceNotes: The linked 2026-2027 call and eligible-country list PDFs were not fetched; degree levels, fields and eligible nationalities are therefore left unknown rather than inferred.
records.evidence: Scholarships are available for attending academic courses on the Italian territory only.

records.name: Invest Your Talent in Italy
records.providerName: Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation
records.summary: Invest Your Talent in Italy offers foreign students Master's and postgraduate courses at Italian universities in Engineering/Advanced Technologies, Architecture/Design, and Economics and Management, with on-the-job training at Italian companies. Courses are taught entirely in English, and selected grantees receive a nine-month scholarship; applications for 2027–2028 were not yet open at the time of verification.
records.sourcePublisher: Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation
records.sourceNotes: The official page describes the programme for foreign students but does not enumerate eligible nationalities or the scholarship amount.
records.evidence: The selected grantees will receive a nine-month scholarship as a contribution to their Italian experience.

records.name: Italy Runs Towards the Future
records.providerName: Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation
records.summary: Italy Runs Towards the Future provides scholarships for young student-athletes from ten listed countries to enroll in Italian-language Master's programmes in Sport Science and Techniques or Sport Management at the University of Rome 'Foro Italico'. For 2026-2027, MAECI offers up to 20 scholarships of €9,000 each for nine months beginning 1 October 2026.
records.sourcePublisher: Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation
records.evidence: For the 2026-2027 academic year, the MAECI will offer up to 20 scholarships worth €9,000 each. These scholarships will have a duration of 9 months, beginning on October 1, 2026.

records.name: University of Helsinki Scholarship Programme
records.summary: The University of Helsinki scholarship programme offers 50% or 100% tuition fee waivers to excellent tuition fee-liable students from outside the EU/EEA and Switzerland who are admitted to a Master's programme. Waivers last two years, require full-time study, and do not cover living expenses; no tuition fee waivers are offered for English-language Bachelor's programmes.
records.sourceNotes: The official page defines eligibility by tuition-fee liability for non-EU/EEA and Swiss citizens without permanent residence in Finland rather than enumerating eligible nationalities.
records.evidence: University of Helsinki scholarship programme consists of tuition fee waivers, waiving the tuition fee for 50 % or 100 %.

records.name: ARES International Training Scholarships
records.providerName: ARES (Académie de recherche et d'enseignement supérieur)
records.summary: ARES International Training Scholarships support permanent residents and workers in 32 eligible partner countries who hold a graduate degree and relevant professional experience. For 2027-2028 the programme offered a specialised bachelor's degree, eight specialised master's degrees and a six-month continuing training certificate in Belgium, with travel, subsistence, insurance and, for degree courses, tuition covered.
records.sourceNotes: The 2027-2028 call was closed at verification; the next call is August 2027. Palestinian nationals are eligible even if they do not reside in an eligible country. Funding components differ by training type, so no single FULLY_FUNDED or PARTIAL category fits.
records.evidence: The scholarship includes international travel expenses, a subsistence allowance, insurance costs, and tuition fees only for bachelor's degrees and specialised master's degrees.

records.name: KTH Scholarship
records.summary: The KTH Scholarship covers the full tuition fee for a one- or two-year Master's programme at KTH for fee-paying students who apply to KTH as their first priority. Selection focuses on academic excellence and motivation to contribute to sustainable development; living costs are not included.
records.sourceNotes: Eligibility is based on fee-paying status and first-priority application rather than nationality; the official page does not enumerate eligible nationalities.
records.evidence: The KTH Scholarship covers the full tuition fee of a one or two year master's programme.

records.name: KTH India Scholarship
records.summary: The KTH India Scholarship Foundation awards one scholarship in 2027 to an Indian citizen who completed an undergraduate programme in India and applies to a fee-paying Master's programme at KTH as first priority. It covers tuition for the first and second year and includes a monthly living allowance during the academic year (10 months).
records.sourceNotes: Not available for joint master's programmes or programmes with obligatory exchange studies; applicants from Mumbai Metropolitan Area and Pune are prioritised under the foundation's statutes.
records.evidence: The scholarship also includes a monthly living allowance during the academic year (10 months).

records.name: WU Excellence Scholarship
records.summary: The WU Excellence Scholarship is an invitation-only award for excellent international MSc students from 22 listed non-EU/EFTA countries who are admitted to an eligible on-campus Master's programme at Wageningen University & Research. It consists of a tuition fee waiver for the 24-month programme; recipients still pay remaining costs such as living allowance, insurance and residence permit fees.
records.sourceNotes: The named scholarship appears in a dedicated section of the official Master's scholarships page. Selection includes a lottery among final-stage candidates; a complete MSc application was due before 1 December 2026.
records.evidence: A tuition fee waiver for the duration of the programme (24 months).

records.name: Africa Scholarship Programme
records.summary: The Africa Scholarship Programme offers talented and motivated citizens of African countries a Master's degree at Wageningen University & Research, with the aim of supporting capacity building in Africa. It covers travel to and from the Netherlands, a 24-month living allowance, 24 months of tuition fees, and visa and health insurance costs.
records.sourceNotes: The named scholarship appears in a dedicated section of the official Master's scholarships page. The official page says 'citizen of an African country' but does not enumerate countries; no country list was inferred.
records.evidence: Travel to and from The Netherlands; living allowance for the duration of the programme (24 months); tuition fee coverage for the duration of the programme (24 months); visa costs and costs for health insurance.

records.name: Anne van den Ban Fund Scholarship
records.summary: The Anne van den Ban Fund supports talented students from low-income and lower-middle-income countries listed by the fund to study at Wageningen University & Research. Invitation-only awards are combined with the WU Fellowship Programme and may cover travel, a 24-month living allowance, 24 months of tuition, and visa and health insurance costs; the award may be partial or full.
records.sourceTitle: Selection Anne van den Ban Fund
records.sourceNotes: The official page states the award may be partial or full, so it is classified as OTHER rather than FULLY_FUNDED or PARTIAL. Selection is by invitation only; a complete MSc application was due before 1 December 2026.
records.evidence: The scholarship may consist of a partial or full scholarship and is only available to prospective students.

records.name: Radboud Scholarship Programme
records.summary: The Radboud Scholarship Programme offers highly motivated non-EEA students with outstanding results a partial scholarship for a complete English-taught Master's programme at Radboud University. It reduces the tuition fee to €2,771 (amount to be confirmed) for 2027/2028 and covers visa, residence permit, health and liability insurance, but not living costs.
records.sourceNotes: Eligibility is stated as holding a non-EU/non-EEA passport; the official page does not enumerate eligible countries.
records.evidence: A Radboud Scholarship will reduce your tuition fee to €2,771.- (amount to be confirmed).

records.name: ASML Technology Scholarship
records.summary: The ASML Technology Scholarship supports students at Radboud University pursuing one of five technical Master's programmes, offering €5,000 per academic year for two years along with a personal ASML mentor and a professional development programme. It is open to students of all nationalities with an average grade of at least 7 and extracurricular activities demonstrating motivation.
records.sourceNotes: The official Radboud page states that full terms, application process, selection and deadlines are on the ASML website; those details were not fetched for this record.
records.evidence: The scholarship offers €5,000 per academic year (for two years), along with access to a personal ASML mentor and a professional development programme.

records.name: Fulbright-Radboud Scholarships
records.summary: Fulbright-Radboud Scholarships are offered to excellent American students for graduate study or research in English-taught Master's and Research Master's programmes at Radboud University. For 2027-2028 one scholarship is available, with monthly instalments of €1,750 and travel reimbursement; tuition fees are not waived.
records.sourceNotes: US students with both US and Dutch or EU citizenship, and US students already residing in the Netherlands, are not considered.
records.evidence: The grant will be paid in 11 monthly installments of €1,750. International travel will be reimbursed to a maximum of €1,000.

records.name: Mahmoud S. Rabbani Scholarship
records.providerName: Lutfia Rabbani Foundation and Radboud University
records.summary: The Mahmoud S. Rabbani Scholarship promotes academic excellence and cultural exchange between Europe and the Arab world. It is intended for Arab students pursuing a Master's or PhD programme in the Netherlands and for Dutch students pursuing a Master's or PhD programme in an Arab country, subject to admission and foundation requirements.
records.sourceNotes: The Radboud page does not state the award amount or coverage; more information is linked to the Lutfia Rabbani Foundation. Eligible countries are taken from the official country/region list on the Radboud page.
